items.text: The page copy is at least 30% shorter: the rendered text inside <main> (hero, features, how it works, pricing, FAQ, closing call to action; header and footer excluded) is at most 809 words, down from 1156.
No "seamless(ly)", "leverage" or "unlock" (any form) anywhere in the rendered page or its title.
No emoji anywhere in the rendered page or its title.
No em-dash bullet stacks: no two consecutive rendered lines start with an em or en dash.
The pricing section still names the Hobby, Team and Business plans with their prices (free, $24, $99).

Every one of these facts is still on the page and unchanged (wording can change and a fact can be stated more briefly, but none is dropped, contradicted or made vaguer): (1) Tidewatch monitors websites and APIs and alerts you when they go down; (2) checks run every 30 seconds from 6 regions (Hobby: every 5 minutes); (3) an alert only goes out after 2 regions confirm the failure; (4) alerts go to email, SMS, Slack and PagerDuty; (5) public status pages on your own domain with your logo and colors, updated automatically from your monitors; (6) setup is pasting a URL (no agent to install) and picking alert channels, about 2 minutes; (7) Hobby: free, 5 monitors, checks every 5 minutes, email alerts, 1 status page; (8) Team: $24/month, 50 monitors, 30-second checks from 6 regions, SMS/Slack/PagerDuty alerts, 5 seats, 1 year of history; (9) Business: $99/month, 500 monitors, SSO (SAML), unlimited seats, 99.9% uptime SLA; (10) yearly billing gives 2 months free; (11) 14-day free trial of the Team plan, no credit card needed; (12) cancel any time from account settings, unused part of the billing period refunded (prorated); (13) data is stored in the EU (Frankfurt) or US (Virginia) region of your choice and never leaves it; (14) a monitor's check history can be exported as CSV. Filler claims (e.g. "thousands of happy teams", "world-class support") may be dropped, and no new product claims are added.

The copy reads like a person wrote it: plain, specific sentences instead of stacked marketing clichés (e.g. "next-generation", "empower", "best-in-class", "supercharge", "world-class", "paradigm", "single pane of glass", "journey"), and headings and buttons say plainly what the section or action is.

_note: Script items build the site, serve dist/ with `vite preview` and read the rendered page in headless Chromium (<details> opened). Generated from one probe prelude per item; keep the five in sync.
